fault: Trial r16 reached its goal and then never terminated. The observer's spin thread (ExecutorPump, added at 0e71dd3) was inside EventHandler.is_ready, where rclpy finalized an action client: rcl_action_client_fini -> rmw_dds_common remove_client_graph -> __rmw_publish -> RTPSWriter::send_nts, blocked in pthread_mutex_lock. That native call does not release the GIL, so the main thread, waiting in ExecutorPump.wait_until, sat in pthread_cond_timedwait for the GIL and could not test its deadline. The 600 s wall backstop was 489 s overdue (monotonic 6187.6 against a deadline of 5698.0) while the trial's simulation ran on past 530 s of a 300 s simulated deadline. This is the same failure class as roundtrip_watchdog_unreachable.json: the 0e71dd3 fix moved spinning off the waiting thread, which bounds a wedge in Python but not one that holds the GIL.

fix.isolation: mission_batch runs every trial's observer through mission_trial.execute_mission_isolated, which calls execute_mission in a spawned child process (isolated_call.run_isolated). The parent holds no ROS participant, waits on a pipe, and kills the child once wall_watchdog_s + 120 s is overdue, recording infrastructure_failure, which is already retryable. Every in-process backstop is kept inside the child.
fix.side_effect: Each trial now gets a fresh DDS participant, so no participant persists across trials to carry state from one stack into the next.
fix.regression_tests: tests/test_isolated_call.py holds the GIL through ctypes.PyDLL, which reproduces the wedge; tests/test_spin_pump.py's wedge sleeps in Python, which releases the GIL and could not. One test measures the in-process backstop arriving late by the GIL hold; another shows the isolated call killing a child wedged in a GIL-holding native call at its limit.
fix.end_to_end_smoke: One round-trip trial through the isolated observer, uncommitted tree, --allow-dirty, results/qualification/smoke_isolated_raw: completed, 0 collisions, 155.93 s simulated, both motion qualifications recorded, no transport errors, no surviving processes.
